clips.text_zh: 成日都係咁，睇BTC橫行幾星期唔理，佢一爆15%就人人衝入去。點解永遠都係泵完先追？等佢回一回先啦，唔好又做最後一個接貨嘅人🙏
clips.text_en_b1: You watch BTC do nothing for weeks and ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened? This comes up on /biz/ every single cycle and nobody learns.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread questioning why people chase BTC after it pumps

signal.rationale: Post-hoc observation on herd behaviour, no actionable setup

clips.text_en_b2: You sit on your hands while BTC trades in a sideways range for weeks, dismissing the whole thing. Then it rips 15% in a single move and the FOMO crowd piles in chasing green candles. Why does nobody manage to buy before the breakout, rather than after the easy money has already been made? The cycle plays out identically on /biz/ every single time, and yet retail traders keep learning absolutely nothing from history, ending up as exit liquidity for smarter participants.
clips.text_en_c1: Anyone who has spent even a cursory amount of time observing Bitcoin's price action will recognise this recurring pattern almost on instinct: BTC consolidates sideways for weeks on end, drawing nothing but indifference, and then once it finally breaks upward with a roughly fifteen percent move, the retail herd piles in with remarkable synchronicity. The question worth posing is why market participants, time and again, position themselves at the tail end of an established trend. Let price retrace, exercise the discipline, and refrain from becoming the final bagholder who absorbs someone else's exit liquidity.
clips.text_en_c2: It is a phenomenon so recurrent it has acquired the texture of ritual: Bitcoin meanders sideways for weeks on end, drawing nothing but indifference from the retail crowd, until the moment it suddenly lurches fifteen percent higher — at which point every self-styled contrarian scrambles to pile in, convinced the locomotive has just left the station. The absurdity lies not in the buying itself but in its timing; participants are perpetually arriving after the move has been thoroughly consummated, mistaking momentum for opportunity. This exact lament resurfaces on /biz/ with metronomic regularity at the tail of every cycle, and yet the lessons, such as they are, evaporate almost as quickly as the gains they purport to explain.

clips.text_zh: 買Cybercab放落Tesla Robotaxi network等收錢，聽落好夢幻喎。一架車成本幾錢？回本期幾耐？計埋保險同維修，係咪真係work？等大佬redpill一下先🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Redpill me on buying Cybercabs and putting them to work on the Tesla Robotaxi network for passive income. How much does each unit cost, what's the realistic payback period, and does the math actually work after insurance and maintenance?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking how to make passive income from Tesla Cybercabs

signal.rationale: Implied bullish on TSLA Robotaxi economics; OP exploring yield-style exposure to the network

clips.text_en_b2: I'm trying to get a realistic picture of the Cybercab opportunity before I throw any capital at it. Putting one of these units on the Tesla Robotaxi network for passive income sounds appealing on paper, but I want to know the real numbers: how much does each vehicle actually cost, what is a sensible timeframe for breaking even, and after you factor in insurance premiums, charging costs, and ongoing maintenance, does the business case genuinely hold up?
clips.text_en_c1: The proposition of purchasing a Cybercab, deploying it onto Tesla's forthcoming Robotaxi network, and thereby generating a steady stream of residual income admittedly sounds rather appealing on paper. Before anyone commits capital, however, several variables warrant rigorous scrutiny: the per-unit acquisition cost, the projected amortisation timeline, and crucially whether the underlying unit economics remain viable once insurance premiums, routine maintenance, depreciation, and platform fees have been factored into the equation. Strip away the marketing veneer, run the numbers in good faith, and only then determine whether the thesis genuinely holds water.
clips.text_en_c2: The proposition is beguiling in its simplicity: acquire a Cybercab, enrol it in Tesla's nascent Robotaxi network, and thereafter collect what purports to be fully passive income while the vehicle earns its keep around the clock. Yet the arithmetic underpinning such fantasies tends to be conspicuously absent from the marketing materials. What, precisely, does a single unit cost at retail, and over what plausible horizon does the cumulative revenue exceed that outlay? Once insurance premiums, depreciation, software subscriptions, and routine maintenance are folded into the spreadsheet, the proposition frequently inverts from income stream to liability. The Tesla faithful are nevertheless eager to be redpilled — though one suspects the red pill, in this instance, dissolves on the tongue rather than illuminating anything. A sober unit-economics breakdown would be vastly more welcome than another glossy reveal.

clips.text_zh: 2016年Hinton話AI 5至10年會取代放射科醫生。10年後啦喎，呢個位請多咗人，仲加薪添。睇完條片我笑咗，佢都係神棍一名lol。下一個出醜嘅應該係Elon🙏
clips.text_en_b1: In 2016, Geoffrey Hinton predicted AI would replace radiologists within 5 to 10 years. It is now 10 years later and there are more radiologists now, in higher demand and earning much higher salaries than in 2016. Next up to embarrass himself on the world stage is probably Elon Musk.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread calling out Hinton's failed radiologist prediction

signal.rationale: Cultural commentary on AI doomers, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2016, Geoffrey Hinton confidently predicted that AI would render radiologists obsolete within a five-to-ten-year window. Roughly a decade has now passed, and the specialty has not collapsed; in fact, demand has actually grown, with higher salaries and more positions filled than ever. Watching his interview back is genuinely cringeworthy, since he is now widely regarded as just another overhyped prophet. My money is on Elon Musk being the next figure to embarrass himself publicly in a similar fashion.
clips.text_en_c1: Back in 2016, Geoffrey Hinton, a figure widely regarded as one of the principal architects of modern deep learning, asserted with considerable authority that artificial intelligence would displace radiologists within a window of five to ten years. A full decade has since elapsed, and the actual outcome has proved rather different from what was forecast: demand for radiologists has in fact risen, salaries have appreciated substantially, and the discipline continues to expand. Such prognostications are best treated with measured scepticism. Should the next public embarrassment arise, my money would be on Elon Musk overpromising once again.
clips.text_en_c2: A decade ago, Geoffrey Hinton — a man routinely described, without irony, as the godfather of modern deep learning — took to a prominent stage and confidently prophesied that radiologists would be rendered obsolete within five to ten years, displaced by convolutional networks capable of inferring malignancy from pixels with superhuman fidelity. Ten years on, the specialty has not merely persisted but expanded: demand for qualified radiologists has surged, compensation has climbed appreciably, and the ranks of residency programmes have swollen rather than thinned. Watching Hinton revisit those remarks on camera is to witness a masterclass in dignified revisionism, delivered with the aplomb of a man accustomed to audiences suspending disbelief. The next luminary slated for comparable public discomfiture is, in all likelihood, Elon Musk, whose own predictions have aged with comparable grace.

clips.text_zh: 有個incel屌鳩班印度人，話人哋inbred又廢。睇完好尷尬，咁都要寫段長文去鬧，現實生活有幾失敗先要噉⁉️唔好理啲incel啦，浪費時間lol
clips.text_en_b1: An incel is seething online at Indians, calling them inbred social outcasts who contribute nothing to society. Reading the post is genuinely painful — nobody writes that much rage unless their own life is falling apart. Just ignore these losers and move on.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread of an incel raging at successful Indian people

signal.rationale: General news vibe, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Some incel is losing his mind online, ranting about Indians and labelling them inbred outcasts who contribute nothing to society at all. Reading the post is honestly uncomfortable, because nobody writes a wall of text that bitter unless their own life is quietly falling apart behind the screen. The irony is that his supposed targets are out building careers and families while he fumes in his bedroom. Honestly, just scroll past these losers and don't waste another second on them.
clips.text_en_c1: An incel has chosen to vent his frustrations online, directing a remarkably prolonged diatribe at Indians, whom he characterises as inbred and socially worthless. The sheer length and intensity of the post are themselves diagnostic — nobody expends that level of emotional energy crafting a screed unless their own circumstances are quietly unravelling. The subtext, as is so often the case, reveals far more about the author's predicament than about the supposed targets of his ire. Best to scroll past and conserve one's attention for more worthwhile pursuits.
clips.text_en_c2: Somewhere on the internet, an incel has committed several hundred words to denouncing Indians as inbred pariahs whose collective contribution to civilisation hovers somewhere between negligible and contemptible. The post is a small masterpiece of projection: nobody, one reflects, drafts a screed of such furious, frothing length unless their own circumstances have curdled beyond the point of dignified silence. There is something almost archaeological about the genre — these texts read less like arguments than like artefacts exhumed from a psyche in chronic distress. The temptation to engage, to refute, to extract some morsel of substantive claim worth contesting, is best resisted entirely; the discourse, such as it is, terminates only when the audience stops listening. Move along, in other words, and conserve your energy for more tractable fools.

clips.text_zh: Riot今次個造型真係做到嘢，條線條色完全唔同level。S15搞到咁靚，唔知打排位會唔會分心lolbtw我隻打野角色都想要新skin🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Riot clearly knew exactly what they were doing with this design. The lines, the colour palette, the silhouette — everything hits differently. Honestly, if they keep dropping skins like this through S15, ranked is going to be very distracting.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread praising Riot's new champion skin design

signal.rationale: Gossip on a League skin, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Riot absolutely nailed the aesthetic on this one, and it honestly shows on every level. The linework, the colour palette, the silhouette, the subtle textures — everything reads as a meaningful step up from anything they have put out recently. If they keep dropping designs at this standard throughout the rest of Season 15, ranked queues are going to feel a lot more like a fashion showcase than an actual competitive match. Btw, my jungler is long overdue for a skin.
clips.text_en_c1: Riot Games have evidently devoted considerable creative energy to this particular skin, and the result speaks for itself: the linework, the chromatic palette, the silhouette — every constituent element operates at a markedly elevated tier relative to their usual output. Should they maintain this standard throughout the duration of Season 15, ranked queues are likely to become considerably more distracting, given that players will presumably be spending an inordinate amount of time admiring their freshly acquired cosmetics rather than attending to the minimap. My jungler could certainly use something equally striking.
clips.text_en_c2: Credit where it is due: Riot's design team has, with this particular release, executed something approaching a masterclass in visual coherence. The linework, the chromatic palette, the silhouette — every constituent element has been calibrated with an evident deliberateness that elevates the entire skin above its peers. Where so many cosmetic releases collapse into chromatic noise, this one demonstrates a discipline that borders on architectural, the kind of restraint that distinguishes a competent artist from a genuinely considered one. Whether such standards can be sustained across an entire competitive season remains to be seen, of course, but if S15 maintains this baseline, ranked queues may well become aesthetically hazardous — players distracted not by ganks but by the sheer pleasure of glancing at their own loadout. Meanwhile, the jungler awaits his own resplendent update.

clips.text_zh: 睇到自己個frame真係頂癮，5呎9 160lbs shoulder又細。樓主話要特別加操肩，我覺得ok但唔好本末倒置，big 3先係重點。肥仔信話佢OHP就嚟1pl8，我連pl8都未掂🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Picrel is my physique. I am 5'9, 160lbs, lifting for 2 years, started skinnyfat at 140, bulked to 200, then cut to here. My frame is small so I put extra emphasis on shoulders, but the big three lifts still matter way more. Diet is dialed at 2293 cals.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking for advice on skinny frame lifting
clips.text_en_b2: Picrel is my current physique — I'm 5'9, 160lbs, about two years into serious lifting. I started skinnyfat at 140, bulked up to 200, then trimmed back down, so I am fully aware of how narrow my frame actually is. Because of that I have been pushing extra shoulder volume, although I refuse to lose sight of the bigger picture: progressive overload on the squat, bench, and deadlift still drives ninety percent of the results. Diet is sitting at 2293 cals.
clips.text_en_c1: The image depicts my current physique, and I shall enumerate the relevant variables: I stand five-foot-nine, currently weigh approximately one hundred and sixty pounds, and have been training consistently for two years. I commenced my journey as a skinnyfat novice at one hundred and forty pounds, gradually bulked up to two hundred, and subsequently cut down to my present weight. My skeletal frame being somewhat modest in proportion, I have elected to allocate additional volume to shoulder work, though I remain firmly cognisant that the compound lifts — squat, bench, deadlift — ought to constitute the bulk of any well-structured programme.
clips.text_en_c2: The photograph in question depicts a physique that is, by any objective measure, workmanlike rather than impressive — five-foot-nine, one hundred and sixty pounds, two years of consistent training distilled into a frame that remains stubbornly narrow across the clavicles. The poster, evidently self-aware of this structural limitation, has elected to allocate disproportionate volume to overhead pressing and lateral work, a compensatory strategy that is not unreasonable in principle but risks inverting the proper hierarchy of priorities. The compound lifts — squat, bench, deadlift — remain the indisputable engine of any serious hypertrophy programme, and aesthetics, however seductive as a goal, must be subordinate to strength.

clips.text_en_b2: Looks like a Norwegian retailer just quietly listed Monolith Soft as the developer handling the Zelda OoT remake for the Switch 2, and honestly the timing lines up suspiciously well with the earlier Switch 2 controller leak and their recent recruitment push. Taken together, the remake is basically a foregone conclusion at this point. If they manage to upscale the original visuals several times over, I would happily rebuy it without a second thought. clips.text_en_c1: A Norwegian retailer has recently listed Monolith Soft as the designated development studio for an anticipated Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake targeting the forthcoming Switch 2 hardware. This particular data point dovetails neatly with the previously leaked Switch 2 controller logo, as well as with the studio's conspicuous recruitment activity over recent quarters. Taken in aggregate, these indicators render the remake effectively confirmed, barring any formal announcement from Nintendo themselves. Provided the visuals receive the substantial upgrade many have been quietly hoping for, a re-purchase would scarcely require any deliberation whatsoever.
clips.text_en_c2: The rumour mill, that inexhaustible engine of Nintendo speculation, has once more disgorged something sufficiently credible to merit attention: a Norwegian retailer, in a momentary lapse of corporate discretion, has apparently listed Monolith Soft as the developer entrusted with the Ocarina of Time remake for the forthcoming Switch 2. The detail dovetails rather too neatly with the previously leaked controller insignia and Monolith's own conspicuous recruitment patterns to be dismissed as coincidence — the convergence of evidence, taken in aggregate, renders outright denial increasingly untenable. Should the visuals receive the generational upgrade the hardware would permit, a re-purchase becomes almost a foregone conclusion, however cynical one might wish to remain.
